thread:
Maya: heads-up: several customers opened tickets about spikes of 5xx and elevated latencies hitting hosted inference endpoints (~07:40 UTC). Support captured one sample error from a customer (Ryan):

Ryan: got back HTTP/1.1 502 and body: {\"error\":\"control-plane: upstream timeout\"} when calling /v1/generate. SDK retrying made things noisier.

Maya: tagging eng-oncall and infra. Can someone take lead?

Sam: oncall here. I see a sharp jump in 5xx starting 07:38:50 UTC for routes that touch control-plane services. Gateway logs show repeated timeouts to controlplane.internal:443.

Sam: quick log tails from control-plane pods (snips):
```
2026-02-02T07:39:02Z ERROR auth-service request_id=def456 timeout waiting for db after 12s
2026-02-02T07:39:03Z ERROR routing-policy request_id=ghi789 db_conn_pool_exhausted
2026-02-02T07:39:05Z WARN config-db slow query: duration=4.2s stmt=\"SELECT ... JOIN ...\"
```

Zara: metrics show config-db active connections pegged at max, auth-service threads blocked on session lookups, routing-policy latencies skyrocketed. Hypothesis: a routing-policy change is causing heavy synchronous DB work.

Alex: context: we shipped routing-policy v2 yesterday with a new policy aggregation. Could be related.

Sam: repro steps I'm using to trace a request:
1) curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.host/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" -d '{\"input\":\"test\"}'
2) watch gateway logs and correlate request_id with control-plane logs

Gateway sample response seen:
```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
{\"error\":\"control-plane: routing-policy timeout\"}
```

Zara: immediate options: 1) rollback routing-policy to previous revision; 2) temporarily increase db pool and add read replica; 3) implement a short-circuit default policy on config-db timeout (fail-open). Which do we prefer for fast remediation?

Sam: I'm initiating a canary rollback to routing-policy v1 at 10% traffic. DeployBot: start rollback.

DeployBot: @Sam rollback started for routing-policy -> v1-canary. Canary 10% traffic.

~5 minutes later

Sam: 5xx rate dropping for routes impacted by routing-policy. Auth timeouts reduced. Canary looks healthy.

Zara: DB connection pool utilization dropped ~65% after traffic shifted. Root cause appears to be an expensive JOIN introduced in v2 plus lack of prepared statements leading to parse/plan overhead. Queries serialized under load.

Alex: we'll revert v2 and schedule a follow-up to optimize the query (use prepared statements, index, paging). Also add pre-deploy checks for query plan regressions.

Maya: customer status update draft for Ryan: \"We found a regression in a control-plane routing-policy deployment that caused DB connection saturation and resulted in 5xx responses between 07:38:50 - 07:59:10 UTC. We rolled back the change and services are stable. We'll provide billing credits for affected requests.\"

Ryan: thanks. can you confirm exact time window and whether any client-side retries caused duplicate billed requests? We saw SDK retries.

Sam: our timeline: incident window 07:38:50 -> 07:59:10 UTC per gateway logs. We'll produce per-customer error counts and token usage during the window. Note: some retries succeeded after rollback; we'll separate retried successful requests for billing purposes.

Jess: billing here 1 will prepare credits once we have the affected-token lists and counts. Please include whether responses were 5xx (no bill) vs success after retry (bill applies).

Zara: immediate action items (SRE):
- postmortem with RCA (query + missing prepared stmt)  Zara owning
- add pre-deploy explain-analyze gate for routing-policy SQL changes  Sam owning
- temporary increase db pool + add read replica planning  infra team
- add fail-open circuit in routing-policy on DB timeouts (max degrade path)

Sam: also adding a short-term metric alert: if config-db p95 > 2s or active_connections > 80% -> trigger paging to oncall.

DeployBot: rollback complete; canary health checks passed; 100% traffic shifted to v1.

Maya: support will collect the list of impacted customers and hand to billing. Engineering to postmortem and push a fix. Tagging owners: @Zara @Sam @Alex @Jess.

Zara: i'll draft initial incident timeline and share in #postmortems within 24 hours.

Maya: thanks team. :thumbsup:
